biography: Munjal Savla's racing journey began not on a track, but on the bustling streets of Mumbai, weaving through traffic on his father's old scooter. The thrill of navigating chaos ignited a passion that led him to local karting events. Lacking the financial backing of many of his peers, Munjal's early career was a testament to his resourcefulness, often spending nights tinkering with engines salvaged from junkyards. His raw talent eventually caught the eye of VW Virtus GTS, offering him a chance in national touring car series. A defining moment came at the Chennai Grand Prix in 2018, where he secured a surprise podium finish. However, his inconsistent performances and a string of recent mechanical failures have put his future with the team in jeopardy. Now at 36, Munjal fights to stay relevant in a sport dominated by younger, more consistent drivers, battling not only his rivals but also the creeping awareness that his peak may have passed.
drivingStyle: Munjal's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward approach characterized by aggressive overtakes and late braking. He thrives on the edge, often pushing his car beyond its limits in qualifying to secure a favorable grid position. While this strategy can lead to spectacular results, it also makes him prone to errors and tire degradation, particularly in longer races. He struggles with tire management, often burning through his rubber early, leading to a significant drop in pace in the latter stages. Under pressure, Munjal tends to become more erratic, either pulling off a miraculous save or spinning out spectacularly.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days, fueled by numerous on-track collisions and accusations of unfair tactics.
A more recent rivalry, born out of Priya consistently outperforming Munjal despite driving a theoretically inferior car. Munjal accuses her of benefiting from team favoritism.
Vikram is a young up-and-comer threatening to take Munjal's seat in VW Virtus GTS. The two have clashed over sponsors and track position.

quirks: Always wears his grandfather's lucky wristband during races, even though it's falling apart.
Insists on listening to a specific Bollywood song ('Chak De! India') right before the start of every race.
Talks to his car before each session, giving it pep talks and apologies in advance.
famousQuote: "Racing is not about perfection; it's about embracing the chaos and finding the rhythm within it."
careerHighlight: His podium finish at the 2018 Chennai Grand Prix, where he started last on the grid due to a qualifying engine failure and fought his way to third, showcasing his exceptional overtaking skills.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2021 Coimbatore Grand Prix, costing him a likely victory and severely damaging his standing within the VW Virtus GTS team.
